quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to check your blind spot if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors show you everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Other drivers will always respond correctly to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider reduce head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A helmet greatly reduces your risk of head and neck injury in a crash. All riders and passengers should wear a DOT-approved helmet.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do with your feet?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
Keep them away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag them or point your toes down, as this can catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: How noticeable is a motorcycle's brake light compared to a car's?

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake light.
Less noticeable than a car's brake light.
Less important than a car's brake light.
More easily seen than a car's brake light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's. Flash your brake light before slowing or stopping to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is the correct body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean forward over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This position lets you reach and operate the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: What should your lane position help you do?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
See others and be seen by them.

questions.correctAnswerText: See others and be seen by them.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should the operator do?

options.text: Keep a longer distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Let air out of the tires for the extra weight.
Do not warn passengers about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger's weight. Keep more space between you and the vehicle ahead when riding with a passenger.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your skills.
You will be safe if you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which surface provides GOOD traction?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement gives the best traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all reduce traction and are more dangerous for motorcycles.

questions.question: What happens when a motorcycle's headlight is on during the day?

options.text: Other drivers do not see it as easily.
Other drivers see it better than when the headlight is off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers see it better than when the headlight is off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. During the day, a motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the BEST traction?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal plates all reduce traction and are more dangerous.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see clearly to the sides.
It has no labels or markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels with the manufacturer's name, instructions, and information about the standards they meet.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you enter traffic.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It can reduce head injury severity.
It makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. It will not block your vision.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility while riding?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle
questions.explanation: To increase visibility, wear bright or reflective clothing. Add extra lights, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed. These actions help other drivers see you.

questions.question: If your footwear has laces, what should you do with them?
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces so they do not catch on your motorcycle while you ride.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, which should you NOT check?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check if they are shiny.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, how can you help others see you?
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance when weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly around your entire head.
The helmet has no cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: When choosing a helmet, make sure it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around your head, and has no damage like cracks or loose padding.

questions.question: A street-legal motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Street-legal motorcycles must have brakes, a headlight, a taillight, a stop lamp, a muffler, a horn, a mirror, and a seat.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding a motorcycle.
